VNA1.claim: The evening Ganga Aarti at Dashashwamedh Ghat lasts about 45 minutes, starting around 6:30 pm in summer and 7 pm in winter.

evidence.quote: The evening aarti lasts around 45 minutes and takes place every day after sunset at 6:30 p.m. in the summer and 7:00 p.m. in the winter. The aarti takes place in the Dashashwamedh ghat

VNA2.claim: Watch from the ghat steps or from a boat, and arrive an hour early for a good spot.

evidence.quote: The visitors can witness the beauty of the aarti from the steps of the ghats, the boats, or the canopy of the Ganga Sewa Nidhi office. However, it is preferable to be at the venue at least an hour ahead of time

VNA3.claim: A morning rowing-boat trip gives the best view of the ghats and their dawn rituals.

evidence.quote: The morning rowing boat trip is one of Varanasi’s must-dos, as it provides the greatest view of the city.
With a sunrise boat trip in the Ganges River, you could immerse yourself in Hindu culture and customs by witnessing the vibrant ceremonies on the ghats at daybreak.

VN1.claim: Varanasi's LBS airport at Babatpur is 22 km from the city and 30 km from Sarnath, with domestic and some international flights.

evidence.quote: Several airlines operates the flights from LBS airport Babatpur which is 22 km. from Varanasi and 30 km. from Sarnath. There is both Domestic and International flights available from Babatpur Airport Varanasi.

PRS1.claim: At the Sangam the brown Ganga meets the green Yamuna, about 7 km from Civil Lines below the ramparts of Akbar's fort.

evidence.quote: This is the point where the brown water of the Ganga meets the green water of the Yamuna, along with the mythical Saraswati, which remains unseen but believed to run underground. It is located about 7 km from Civil Lines, overlooked by the eastern ramparts of the Akbar Fort.

PRS2.claim: Boats to the Sangam can be hired at the ghat near the fort; priests on mid-river platforms help pilgrims with their ritual bath.

evidence.quote: At the mid-river point priests perch on small platforms to perform puja and assist the devout in their ritual ablutions in the shallow waters.
Boats to the Sangam can be rented by pilgrims and tourists alike at the ghat near the fort.

PRS5.claim: Anand Bhawan, built by Motilal Nehru, is a house museum of the Nehru family and has the Jawahar Planetarium.

evidence.quote: The Anand Bhawan is a historic house museum in Allahabad, which belongs to the Nehru family.
The Bhawan houses the Jawahar Planetarium.

AY7.claim: UPSRTC buses run 24 hours; Ayodhya is about 130 km from Lucknow, 160 km from Prayagraj, 200 km from Varanasi and 636 km from Delhi.

evidence.quote: Services of Uttar Pradesh State Road Transport Corporation buses are available 24 hours a day
The city is about 130 k.m. from Lucknow, 200 k.m. from Varanasi, 160 k.m. from Prayagraj , 140 k.m. from Gorakhpur and about 636 k.m. from Delhi.

AYS2.claim: Tradition holds that Hanuman lived here to guard Ayodhya; the temple is said to have been built by Vikramaditya.

evidence.quote: Vikramaditya got a temple constructed which later on came to be known as Hanuman Garhi. It is believed that Lord Hanuman (Pavan Putra) lived here guard Ayodhya.

RM3.claim: The temple trust issues free passes for darshan and aarti and charges no fee for them.

evidence.quote: Trust does not charge any fee for aarti & darshan passes

AYS5.claim: Ram ki Paidi is a series of ghats on the Saryu, floodlit at night, where pilgrims bathe.

evidence.quote: Ram ki Paidi is a series of ghats on the bank of River Saryu. The river front brings forth an outstanding Landscape especially in floodlit night.
These serve as platforms to devotees who it is said, come to wash away their sins by taking a dip in the river.

LKS2.claim: Its central hall is the largest vaulted hall in the world, built without wooden or metal supports.

evidence.quote: the structure’s design eschewed woodwork, except for the interior galleries, and boasts the world’s largest vaulted hall
The central hall, a proof of ingenious engineering, boasts the largest arched roof in the world without any wooden or metal support.

LK7.claim: Chaudhary Charan Singh International Airport is at Amausi, 14 km from the city centre, with direct flights to many Indian cities and the Gulf.

evidence.quote: Situated in Amausi, 14 kilometers from the city’s nucleus, this airport was formerly known as Amausi Airport.
International connections to: Muscat, Dammam, Dubai, Abu Dhabi, Jeddah, Sharjah, Bangkok, Kuala Lumpur, and Ras-al-Khaymah.

UPC_VNPR.claim: Varanasi to Prayagraj is about 125 km by road on NH-19, about 2.5–3 hours.

evidence.quote: The distance from Varanasi to Prayagraj is 125 km by road via NH-19, and the drive takes about 2.5-3 hours.

UPC_PRAY.claim: Ayodhya is about 170 km from Prayagraj, usually no more than 4 hours by road.

evidence.quote: Travellers also often include sacred Ayodhya in their itinerary, located 170 kilometres away; the road from there to Prayagraj usually takes no more than 4 hours.

VNA4.claim: On Dev Deepavali, the full moon 15 days after Diwali, the ghats are lit with lamps.

evidence.quote: On the full moon 15 nights after Diwali, the holy city celebrates Dev Deepavali

DG1.claim: Dashashwamedh Ghat is known for the Ganga Aarti held every evening.

evidence.quote: Dashashwamedh Ghat is renowned for the spectacular Ganga Aarti held every evening

KV1.claim: The present Kashi Vishwanath Temple, dedicated to Shiva and known as the Golden Temple, was built in 1780 by Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of Indore.

evidence.quote: also known as the Golden temple dedicated to the Lord Shiva. It was constructed in the year 1780 by the Maratha monarch, Maharani Ahilyabai Holkar of the Indore.

KV2.claim: The Shri Kashi Vishwanath Corridor, opened in December 2021, connects the temple with the ghats.

evidence.quote: inaugurated the Shri Kashi Vishwanath Corridor project, which aimed to enhance the city's spiritual vibrancy by connecting many ghats to the temple of Kashi Vishwanath, in December 2021

KV3.claim: The temple trust offers 'Sugam Darshan', a booked, queue-less visit with an escort and a free locker.

evidence.quote: Queueless darshan of the Lord, escorted by a Shastri Assistance, Free Locker and concluded with Mewaladdu Prasadam.

VN_KVT.claim: Phones, cameras and bags are not allowed into Kashi Vishwanath; leave them at the lockers outside the entrance.

evidence.quote: Phones, cameras and bags do not go in; the desks and lockers outside the entrance hold them, and the shops in the lane will hold them too for a small charge.

S5.claim: Sarnath is about 8 km north-east of Varanasi.

evidence.quote: Sarnath is located eight kilometres (five miles) northeast of Varanasi

S6.claim: The Dhamekh Stupa is 42 m tall; the Chaukhandi Stupa marks where the Buddha met his first five disciples.

evidence.quote: The Dhamekh Stupa, standing 42 metres tall
Explore Chaukhandi Stupa where Buddha met his first five disciples

VN_SRM.claim: The Sarnath Museum is closed on Fridays; it is open from about 9 or 10 am to 5 pm on other days.

evidence.quote: Closed: Fridays
Timings: 9 AM - 5 PM, Closed on Friday

PRS4.claim: Incredible India lists the Sangam as open 5 am to 7 pm.

evidence.quote: Opening time - 05:00 AM
Closing time - 07:00 PM

PRS6.claim: Next door, Swaraj Bhawan was the original Nehru mansion, where Indira Gandhi was born; it was given to the Indian National Congress in the 1920s.

evidence.quote: It served as the ancestral home of the Nehru family, Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi was born here. In the 1920s, Motilal Nehru donated the house to the Indian National Congress

PRS7.claim: Khusro Bagh is a walled garden with three sandstone Mughal tombs: Prince Khusro (Jahangir's eldest son), his mother Shah Begum and his sister.

evidence.quote: Khusro Bagh is a large historical garden, in which tombs of Prince Khusro, the eldest son of Emperor Jahangir and Sultan Begum are located. The three sandstone mausoleums within this walled garden, represent an exquisite example of Mughal architecture.
Next to the Begum’s tomb is the tomb of Khusrau’s sister, Nithar.

PRS11.claim: Near the Sangam in Daraganj, the Lete Hue (reclining) Hanuman temple has a 20-foot south-facing idol of Hanuman lying down.

evidence.quote: It is believed that this strange statue of Hanuman is south-facing and 20 feet long.
he lay down here on the banks of the Sangam

PR4.claim: The Magh Mela is held every year from mid-January to mid-February, starting on Makar Sankranti, with a tented township at the Sangam.

evidence.quote: This Mela is held every year during the Hindu month of Magh (corresponding from mid January – mid February) and the important bathing dates are spread over a period of 45 days. It commences on the day of Makar Sankranti in January, which is the first important bathing day.

AYS1.claim: Hanuman Garhi is 1 km from Ayodhya railway station; its main shrine has an idol of the child Hanuman on his mother Anjani's lap.

evidence.quote: Hanuman Garhi is 1 km from Ayodhya railway station.
You will find here a beautiful idol of Bal (young) sitting on lap of Maa Anjani at the main temple.

AYS3.claim: Kanak Bhawan, north-east of Ram Janmabhoomi, is believed to have been Kaikeyi's gift to Sita; the sanctum holds idols of Ram and Sita.

evidence.quote: Kanak Bhawan is to the north-east of Ram Janam Bhumi, Ramkot, in Ayodhya.
It is believed that this Bhawan was gifted to Devi Sita by Kaikei immediately after her marriage to Lord Ram.
The main idols installed in the garbhgrih (sanctum), are of Lord Ram and Devi Sita.

RM2.claim: The temple is built entirely of stone in the Nagara style; the 51-inch Ram Lalla idol stands in the sanctum.

evidence.quote: The Ram Mandir in Ayodhya is made entirely of stone
The 51-inch-tall Ram Lalla idol in the temple's sanctum sanctorum

RM4.claim: The trust lists Mangal Aarti at 4:30 am, Shringar Aarti at 6:30 am and Shayan Aarti at 9:30 pm.

evidence.quote: Mangal Aarti : 04:30 AM
Shringar Aarti : 06:30 AM
Shayan Aarti : 09:30 PM

UP_RMPH.claim: Mobile phones are banned in the Ram temple; the trust asks devotees to leave phones, footwear and purses outside.

evidence.quote: Mobile phones are now banned on the premises of the Ram Temple
The trust advised devotees to leave their mobile phones, footwear, purses, etc., outside the Mandir premises for their convenience and to save time.

UP_LKAY.claim: Lucknow to Ayodhya is about 135 km by road via Barabanki, about 2.5–3 hours.

evidence.quote: The distance from Lucknow to Ayodhya is 135 km by road via NH-330 via Barabanki, and the drive takes about 2.5-3 hours.

LKS1.claim: The Bara (Asafi) Imambara was built between 1784 and 1791 by Nawab Asaf-ud-Daula as a famine-relief project.

evidence.quote: The Asafi Imambada, a iconic landmark in Lucknow, was erected between 1784 and 1791, a period marked by a devastating famine.

LKS4.claim: The Bara Imambara is famous for its Bhul Bhulaiya labyrinth.

evidence.quote: Beyond belief: The Bhul Bhulaiya - A labyrinth of legends

UP_BIF.claim: The Bara Imambara pass costs ₹50 for Indian adults and ₹500 for foreign adults.

evidence.quote: Bara Imambara pass: ₹50 for Indian adults and ₹500 for foreign adults

UP_BIH.claim: Incredible India lists the Bara Imambara as closing at 5 pm and closed on Mondays.
UP_BIH.conflictNote: The managing trust's visitor information is reported as 6 am–6 pm with a Friday closure from 10 am to 3 pm; avoid Mondays and Friday midday.

LKF2.claim: Tunday Kababi, named after its one-armed founding cook, is the place for galouti kebabs; the Aminabad outlet serves mutton as well as beef.

evidence.quote: While the original Tunday Kababi for legendary galouti kebabs is in Chowk, we would recommend the outlet at Aminabad. It has both beef and mutton options, while the one at Chowk dishes out only beef kebabs.

itineraries.title: Uttar Pradesh spiritual circuit in 6 days: Varanasi, Prayagraj, Ayodhya and Lucknow
itineraries.summary: Two days in Varanasi — the Ganga Aarti, a sunrise boat, Kashi Vishwanath and Sarnath — then the Sangam at Prayagraj, Ayodhya's Ram temple and ghats, and Lucknow's Bara Imambara to finish.
itineraries.seoTitle: UP Spiritual Circuit 6 Days: Varanasi, Prayagraj, Ayodhya, Lucknow
itineraries.seoDescription: A one-way six-day Uttar Pradesh pilgrimage with real distances: Varanasi and Sarnath, Prayagraj's Sangam (125 km), Ayodhya (about 170 km) and Lucknow (135 km).

plan.overview: A one-way pilgrimage across eastern Uttar Pradesh: fly into Varanasi and out of Lucknow. Two Varanasi days cover the evening Ganga Aarti, a sunrise boat, Kashi Vishwanath and Sarnath. Day 3 drives 125 km to Prayagraj for Anand Bhawan and Khusro Bagh. Day 4 starts with a boat to the Sangam, where the Ganga meets the Yamuna, then about 170 km to Ayodhya for the floodlit ghats of Ram ki Paidi. Day 5 is Ayodhya's temples; Day 6 drives 135 km to Lucknow for the Bara Imambara and a kebab supper before flying out.
plan.start: Varanasi (LBS airport, 22 km from the city)
plan.end: Lucknow (airport at Amausi, 14 km from the centre)
plan.season: October to March is best. The Magh Mela at Prayagraj's Sangam runs mid-January to mid-February; Dev Deepawali, 15 days after Diwali, lights Varanasi's ghats.
plan.transport: Car with driver Varanasi → Prayagraj → Ayodhya → Lucknow (about 430 km), plus boats and autos locally.

budget.assumptions: Temple darshan passes at Ayodhya are free; boats, guides and hotels vary too much to estimate.

lines.label: Ram Janmabhoomi darshan and aarti passes

booking.detail: One car for Days 3–6, Varanasi to Lucknow; agree the driver's allowance and night stops.
Open-jaw: into Varanasi, out of Lucknow.
Get the free aarti passes from the temple trust ahead of Day 5.

alternatives: Short on time? Skip Prayagraj and drive Varanasi → Ayodhya (about 200 km) on Day 3.
Visiting in Magh Mela season? Stay a night at the Sangam's tented township.
tips: Leave phones at the hotel for Kashi Vishwanath and the Ram temple — neither allows them.
The Sarnath Museum is closed on Fridays; the Bara Imambara on Mondays.
Start road days early to arrive in daylight.

prep.title: Dress and belongings
prep.body: Dress modestly, wear slip-on shoes and carry as little as possible — you'll pass several security checks.

faqs.q: How far is Prayagraj from Varanasi?
faqs.a: About 125 km by road on NH-19, roughly 2.5–3 hours.

faqs.q: How far is Ayodhya from Lucknow?
faqs.a: About 135 km via Barabanki, 2.5–3 hours by road.
